Sumbawa’s Hidden Jungle Escape

What the Agal Waterfall Trek Is Like

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-e4d3a85 elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor

children.html:
Walk jungle trails, cross rivers, and find a hidden waterfall with crystal-clear pools. The two-hour trek is challenging but rewarding, offering the perfect spot to cool off after the journey.

This full-day excursion is made for explorers who love the outdoors. The rugged trails, refreshing waters, and local sights make every step exciting. With plenty of water provided along the way and a satisfying meal at a nearby warung to wrap up the trip, this experience is a chance to connect with nature.

children.html:
Into the Heart of Nature

The Trail: Forest, Rivers and the Falls

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-904bc88 elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html:
The trail to Agal Waterfall winds through lush forests, where towering trees provide shade and birds fill the air with sound. Rocky paths and steady climbs keep the journey exciting, offering a true trek through nature.

As you get closer, river crossings add to the adventure—cool streams flow through the jungle, making for a refreshing challenge. The final reward is the waterfall itself, where clear water cascades into inviting pools, perfect for cooling off and taking in the scenery.

Pack Light

What to Bring

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-6352e1d elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html:
Shoes with grip that you don’t mind getting wet, swimwear under your clothes, a quick-dry towel, sunscreen and a dry bag for your phone. We bring the water. If it’s rained in the past few days, the river crossings run higher, so expect wet knees.

Agal or Kalela? Choosing Your Waterfall

Pick Agal if you want a proper full-day trek with river crossings and a remote feel. Pick Kalela Waterfall if you want something easy: a 30 to 45 minute walk to a tosca-blue pool, done in half a day. Plenty of guests do Kalela first and Agal later in the week.

children.html:
How long is the hike to Agal Waterfall?

About two hours along a jungle trail with several river crossings. With the drive and a meal afterwards, plan for a full day.

Is the Agal Waterfall trek difficult?

It’s challenging rather than technical. Expect rocky paths, steady climbs and wading through streams. Reasonably fit walkers manage it fine with good shoes.

Can you swim at Agal Waterfall?

Yes. The falls drop into clear pools that are good for a swim after the hike.

Do I need a guide for Agal Waterfall?

We recommend one. The trail crosses rivers and isn’t signposted, and a local guide knows where to cross safely when water levels change.

When is the best time to visit Agal Waterfall?

The flow is strongest during and just after the rainy season (November to April). The dry season (May to October) makes the trail and river crossings easier.
